records.title: Blood clot in a vein
records.summary: Swelling, pain or a cord-like vein in the neck or leg.

data.trigger: Swelling, pain or a cord-like vein in the neck or leg.
steps: Start anticoagulant only with flight surgeon agreement
Plan landing and bleeding risk with the ground team
data.comms_note: A jugular vein clot was found in an ISS astronaut during a research scan and was treated in flight.

records.title: Severe low blood sugar (unable to swallow)
records.summary: Confused or unresponsive with low blood sugar.

data.trigger: Confused or unresponsive with low blood sugar.
steps: Do not give anything by mouth

records.title: Swallowed a toxic substance
records.summary: Accidental swallowing of a chemical or medication overdose.

data.trigger: Accidental swallowing of a chemical or medication overdose.
steps: Do not make the person vomit

records.title: Acute anxiety or panic
records.summary: Sudden fear with racing heart, breathlessness or trembling.

data.trigger: Sudden fear with racing heart, breathlessness or trembling.
steps: Slow breathing: 4 seconds in, 6 seconds out
Rule out medical causes: check SpO₂, heart rate and blood sugar
data.escalate: Same day if repeated, or if medication is needed.

records.title: Crew conflict
records.summary: Ongoing tension or arguments affecting work or wellbeing.

data.trigger: Ongoing tension or arguments affecting work or wellbeing.
steps: Pause and separate tasks for a while
Use the agreed crew conflict process
Private conference with ground psychological support
data.comms_note: Small crews on long missions cannot walk away from each other.

records.title: Difficult news from home
records.summary: Bereavement or serious family news received during the mission.

data.trigger: Bereavement or serious family news received during the mission.
steps: Private call with family when the link allows
Adjust workload for the next days
Check in daily on sleep and mood
data.escalate: Next private conference, sooner if needed.
data.comms_note: Comms delay can make real-time support from home impossible.

records.title: Using an expired medicine
records.summary: The only available medicine for a condition has passed its expiry date.

data.trigger: The only available medicine for a condition has passed its expiry date.
steps: Check for a non-expired alternative in the pharmacy
Inspect for discolouration, crumbling or cloudiness
Use per flight surgeon guidance, accepting possible lower potency
data.escalate: Inform the ground at the next contact.
data.comms_note: A 2024 study found most ISS-formulary medicines would expire before a Mars mission ends.

records.title: Medicine running low
records.summary: Two or fewer doses left of a medicine.

data.trigger: Two or fewer doses left of a medicine.
steps: Check pharmacy for alternatives in the same class
Reserve remaining doses for the most serious uses
data.comms_note: Beyond low Earth orbit there is no resupply.

records.title: High cumulative radiation dose
records.summary: Cumulative dose above 50% of the career limit.

data.trigger: Cumulative dose above 50% of the career limit.
steps: Plan EVAs for quiet space weather

records.title: Suit pressure loss during EVA
records.summary: Suit pressure alarm, ear pain or breathlessness during EVA.

data.trigger: Suit pressure alarm, ear pain or breathlessness during EVA.

records.title: Dental abscess
records.summary: Throbbing toothache with swelling of the gum or face.

data.trigger: Throbbing toothache with swelling of the gum or face.
steps: Rinse with warm salt water or chlorhexidine
Temporary filling if a filling is lost
data.escalate: Same day if swelling spreads or fever develops.

records.title: Headache
records.summary: Headache without warning signs.

data.trigger: Headache without warning signs.
steps: Check CO₂ level, hydration and sleep
Rest in a darker, quieter area
data.escalate: Immediately if sudden and severe, or with vision change, weakness or confusion.
data.comms_note: Headaches are common in flight, often linked to CO₂ and fluid shift.

records.title: Suspected sepsis
records.summary: Infection signs plus fast heart rate, low blood pressure, fast breathing or confusion.

data.trigger: Infection signs plus fast heart rate, low blood pressure, fast breathing or confusion.
steps: Measure temperature, heart rate, blood pressure, SpO₂ and breathing rate
Start IV fluids if blood pressure is low
Give a broad-spectrum antibiotic per protocol without waiting
data.comms_note: Sepsis can progress within hours; early antibiotics matter most.

records.title: Chest infection (pneumonia)
records.summary: Cough with fever, breathlessness or chest pain on breathing.

data.trigger: Cough with fever, breathlessness or chest pain on breathing.
steps: Check temperature, SpO₂ and breathing rate
Isolate and clean shared air filters
data.escalate: Same day; immediately if SpO₂ falls below 92%.

records.title: Migraine
records.summary: Throbbing one-sided headache with light sensitivity or nausea.

data.trigger: Throbbing one-sided headache with light sensitivity or nausea.
steps: Rest in a dark, quiet area
data.escalate: Immediately if it is the worst headache ever, or with weakness or vision loss.

records.title: Vertigo after a gravity change
records.summary: Spinning sensation, imbalance or nausea after landing or arriving on a planetary surface.

data.trigger: Spinning sensation, imbalance or nausea after landing or arriving on a planetary surface.
steps: Sit or lie down; avoid fast head turns
Fix your gaze on a stable point
Walk only with a crewmate until steady
data.escalate: If it lasts more than 3 days or comes with hearing loss, weakness or severe headache.

records.title: Persistent insomnia
records.summary: Trouble falling or staying asleep for several nights.

data.trigger: Trouble falling or staying asleep for several nights.
steps: Short-term sleep medication only per protocol
data.escalate: At the next private medical conference.

records.title: Low mood lasting more than two weeks
records.summary: Low mood, loss of interest, poor sleep or withdrawal lasting two weeks or more.

data.trigger: Low mood, loss of interest, poor sleep or withdrawal lasting two weeks or more.
steps: Talk with the crew medical officer privately
Book a private conference with ground psychological support
Plan meaningful tasks and family contact
data.escalate: Same day if there are any thoughts of self-harm.

records.title: Acute radiation exposure
records.summary: Very high dose reading during a solar particle event, or nausea and vomiting after one.

data.trigger: Very high dose reading during a solar particle event, or nausea and vomiting after one.
steps: Move to the storm shelter immediately
Record the time and dosimeter reading
Monitor for fever and bleeding over the next days
data.comms_note: Only a very large solar event without shelter can cause this.

records.title: Low oxygen during EVA
records.summary: Confusion, slurred speech or breathlessness during a spacewalk.

data.trigger: Confusion, slurred speech or breathlessness during a spacewalk.
steps: Return to the airlock with a buddy
Give oxygen and check SpO₂ inside

records.title: Carbon monoxide exposure
records.summary: Headache, nausea or confusion after a fire or equipment fault.

data.trigger: Headache, nausea or confusion after a fire or equipment fault.
steps: Masks on and move to clean air
Do not trust a normal SpO₂: oximeters cannot detect carbon monoxide

records.title: Kidney infection
records.summary: Fever with flank pain, often after urinary symptoms.

data.trigger: Fever with flank pain, often after urinary symptoms.

records.title: Red, sticky eye
records.summary: Red eye with discharge, no vision loss.

data.trigger: Red eye with discharge, no vision loss.
steps: Clean the eyelids with sterile water
Photograph the eye for the flight surgeon
data.escalate: Same day if painful, light sensitive or vision drops.

records.title: Cold injury to fingers or toes
records.summary: Numb, white or hard skin after a cold suit or glove fault.

data.trigger: Numb, white or hard skin after a cold suit or glove fault.

records.title: Mild allergic reaction
records.summary: Itchy rash or hives without breathing problems.

data.trigger: Itchy rash or hives without breathing problems.
steps: Watch for lip, tongue or throat swelling
data.escalate: Immediately if breathing or swallowing is affected (switch to the anaphylaxis protocol).

records.title: Sudden vision loss
records.summary: Sudden loss of vision in one or both eyes.

data.trigger: Sudden loss of vision in one or both eyes.

records.title: Fainting during or after exercise
records.summary: Collapse or near-collapse during or right after exercise.

data.trigger: Collapse or near-collapse during or right after exercise.
steps: Check heart rate, rhythm and blood pressure
data.escalate: Same day; immediately with chest pain.

records.title: Knocked-out tooth
records.summary: A tooth knocked out by impact.

data.trigger: A tooth knocked out by impact.
steps: Hold the tooth by the crown, not the root
Rinse gently and put it back in the socket if possible
Otherwise keep it in saliva or saline

records.title: Wrong dose or wrong medicine given
records.summary: A medicine given in the wrong dose, to the wrong person, or the wrong medicine.

data.trigger: A medicine given in the wrong dose, to the wrong person, or the wrong medicine.
steps: Record what, how much and when
Follow the specific reversal or monitoring advice

records.title: Fatigue before a critical operation
records.summary: Very tired before a docking, EVA or other critical task.

data.trigger: Very tired before a docking, EVA or other critical task.
